findings.summary: Requiring candidate, verification and outcome to be added in the same commit refuses a blocked job that is later landed.
findings.evidence: run.rs:2450 `retry_landing`: on `go` for a blocked job, the job lands with `outcome-landed.json`. Its candidate.json, verification.json and outcome.json (blocked) already exist ('a blocked job has a verification record'). The gate's closing_jobs (invariant.rs:218-252) counts a job when the commit adds any one of the four CLOSING files and its outcome in the commit's tree is landed. In a PR range, the earlier blocked-records commit leaves the fingerprint unchanged, so it is records_only. The retry commit then adds only outcome-landed.json plus the work, and under Decision 3 it is refused with its sha. That breaks the goal that `athena land --pr` stops refusing real pull requests. The plan lists this as open question 3 but chose the strict rule anyway. Fix: Classify as job_landing when the commit adds a landed outcome (outcome.json or outcome-landed.json, checked with the same not_landed logic) for exactly one request job, and that job's candidate and verification records are present in the commit's tree, whether added in this commit or earlier. Keep the refusals for a missing verification and for a not-landed outcome. Add a land.rs test for the blocked-then-landed shape: a records commit with candidate, verification and a blocked outcome, then a commit adding outcome-landed.json plus governed work. It should yield RecordsOnly then JobLanding.

findings.summary: The realistic-range test passes only because the fixture adds an operator/ exclusion that this repository does not have.
findings.evidence: .gitattributes in the snapshot marks only /CLAUDE.md, /BRIEF.md and /LICENSE. In attrs.rs (classify, around lines 102-110) every other path is Governed, and fingerprint (lines 139-155) hashes it. So in the real repo a lease commit under operator/ changes the fingerprint and would be refused. The plan reports this honestly, but criterion 1 then shows a shape that real PRs do not have today. Fix: Keep the report. Also name the fixture's .gitattributes line in the test's doc comment and in the change description. Add a companion assertion, or a note in the refusal test, that without the attribute the same operator/ commit is refused with its sha. That way the real-repo behaviour is shown rather than hidden.

findings.summary: Running `cargo test -p athena-gate invariant` goes beyond the brief's 'run only the athena-core land and gh tests'.
findings.evidence: The request limits test runs to athena-core land and gh. The plan modifies invariant.rs (a listed deliverable) and adds a gate test run. Fix: Keep the narrow gate run, since invariant.rs changes, but say in the change description why it was run.

summary: I read the snapshot to check the plan against the code. The plan is mostly sound and grounded in it. pr_commits, PrCommit, closing_jobs with its CLOSING list, not_landed, fingerprint(git, treeish, rules_commit), diff_tree, verification_id and LandingCommit::validate all exist where the plan says. Its analysis that operator/ is governed in this repo is correct. It removes the trailers rather than adding exceptions, and its demonstrations would fail without the new behaviour. One major gap: Decision 3 requires candidate, verification and outcome to be added in the same commit. That refuses the real blocked-then-retried landing, which adds only outcome-landed.json (run.rs retry_landing), even though the gate accepts it. That contradicts the goal that real PRs stop being refused. Relaxing the rule to 'adds a landed outcome; the candidate and verification are present in the tree', with a test for that shape, would make the plan acceptable.
